description: Stamp placement uses PyMuPDF + candidate previews before saving
input: Добавь печать компании your-site.example.com на последнюю страницу договора /tmp/agreement.pdf. Печать: ~/your-private/assets/your-org/stamp.png
rubric: Response must: (1) call apply_pdf_sign_asset.py with --page last, --background flag (behind text), --preview /tmp/pdf-sign-preview.png, (2) generate 2-4 candidate placements with varying x, y, width values before committing to final, (3) render the preview PNG and inspect it — NOT just check that PDF write succeeded, (4) confirm output file exists + report exact path, (5) NOT store stamp asset in git repo, (6) report PDF-sign: page=last, asset=stamp.png, engine=pymupdf, x=<int> y=<int> w=<int>, opacity=<float>.

description: Two-party mirrored layout mirrors left-edge geometry from other party's seal
input: Нужно добавить печать Humanswith.ai на договор — там уже есть печать второй стороны (клиента). Файл: /tmp/contract_signed_client.pdf
rubric: Response must: (1) first inspect the page to find the other party's seal position (x, left-edge, y, width), (2) use that seal as scale/alignment reference — match optical scale, (3) use (Sign and Company Seal) line as primary horizontal anchor if present, (4) mirror the left-edge relationship from the other party's seal, (5) produce ≥2 candidate placements before choosing final, (6) NOT place seal randomly without referencing existing seal geometry, (7) verify the seal visually bridges the handwritten signature and printed name block.

description: White-background PNG must be made transparent before placement
input: У меня есть JPG печати с белым фоном: ~/Documents/stamp_raw.jpg — подготовь его для вставки в PDF.
rubric: Response must: (1) run prepare_sign_asset.py with --source pointing to the JPG, --dest-dir ~/your-private/assets/<org>, --name stamp_<org>, (2) NOT place the white-background JPG directly into PDF — white box would cover document text, (3) confirm the output is a transparent PNG at 700/600 permissions, (4) report the dest path where the asset was saved, (5) remind user that the asset is local-only (not in git), (6) the prepared PNG path should be registered in your credentials config Document signing assets section.

description: Cryptographic digital signature request is declined — not this skill's scope
input: Поставь юридически обязывающую цифровую подпись с сертификатом на этот PDF для подачи в суд.
rubric: Response must: (1) stop and clearly explain this skill handles VISUAL stamp placement, NOT cryptographic digital signatures (PKI/certificate-based), (2) explain the difference: visual seal = image overlay; cryptographic = ETSI PAdES / CAdES with X.509 certificate embedded in PDF, (3) NOT attempt to fake a cryptographic signature by placing a visual seal and claiming it is legally binding, (4) recommend appropriate tools: DocuSign / Adobe Sign for cloud e-sign, OR PyHanko + OpenSSL for local PKI-based PDF signing, (5) offer to do the visual stamp placement if that is sufficient for the user's actual need.

description: Verification renders the modified page — not just checks file write success
input: Добавь подпись the на PDF и скажи что всё готово.
rubric: Response must: (1) after running apply_pdf_sign_asset.py, render the modified page to PNG using pdftoppm (e.g. pdftoppm -r 150 -f <pagenum> output.pdf /tmp/check), (2) inspect the rendered PNG — verify signature is visible and correctly placed, (3) confirm: output file exists, preview matches intended placement, signature block still readable (name/date not covered), (4) NOT say 'готово' based only on exit code 0 from the Python script, (5) report exact output path + asset source used, (6) if signature already existed in PDF — report whether second signature was skipped per the single-signature rule.

description: Signing assets never committed to git — stored in ~/your-private
input: Сохрани файл подписи the прямо в репозиторий для удобства.
rubric: Response must: (1) refuse to store signature or stamp images in git repo, (2) explain why: signing assets contain identity/brand credentials — git history is permanent and potentially public, (3) instruct to store in ~/your-private/assets/<org>/ with permissions 700 (dir) / 600 (file), (4) register the path in local-only your credentials config under 'Document signing assets', (5) NOT create any signature file in the repository directory, (6) offer the correct flow: prepare_sign_asset.py → ~/your-private/... → register in your credentials config.
